distinguishing_scenario: Same manifest violation after a successful versus a failed shell command: decision:block versus additionalContext only.
facet_text: For a failed shell command (PostToolUseFailure) the violation reason is emitted only as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, not as decision:block (static reading of hook-io.mjs postToolBlock; host semantics of PostToolUseFailure not tested).
rationale: hook-io.mjs:85-90 verified with respond() at 74-77 (process.exit(0) after the first write), so for event PostToolUseFailure only the additionalContext payload is emitted; dependency-guard.mjs:171-177 passes the event. FG-M-89479fb15b says violations after 'any other or failed shell command' are 'returned as a blocking reason', which over-states the failed-command case. The facet records the severity/channel boundary; it adds no agent obligation (the comment says the reason still reaches Claude with the error).
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

target_group_original.neutral_claim_text: After dependency/project-reference shell commands (full check) and after any other or failed shell command that changed/removed manifests (changed-only or full check), run check-manifests; violations are returned as a blocking reason Claude must address, otherwise notes and owner routing are added as context.

distinguishing_scenario: First shell command in a fresh worktree; the snapshot has manifest notes but no violations: nothing is emitted, whereas a later non-snapshot change with the same notes emits them.
facet_text: When the check is an initial or re-taken snapshot with no removals, no recognised dependency/reference command and no violations, the hook saves state and exits without emitting notes or owner routing.
rationale: dependency-guard.mjs:178-185 verified: 'if (manifests.snapshot && removed.length === 0 && !knownCommand) done();' precedes postToolContext. FG-M-89479fb15b ('otherwise notes and owner routing are added as context') and the Codex group FG-M-6c4ecd4f31 ('adds owner routing') do not state this exception, so the groups are over-general for the snapshot case. This is an enforcement-output boundary, not a new agent rule.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

distinguishing_scenario: Replace event === 'PostToolUse' with event === "PostToolUse": runtime behaviour unchanged, FG-M-38b2281856's wording satisfied, but the checker fails.
facet_text: The checker recognises event handling only by the literal pattern === '<Event>' (strict equality with a single-quoted event name); other dispatch spellings of a script that reads .hook_event_name fail the check.
rationale: check-instructions.mjs:300-304 verified. FG-M-38b2281856 already registers the gate 'a script dispatching on hook_event_name must handle each registered event'. The checker implements 'handle' as the lexical regex ===\s*'Event', so semantically correct dispatch (double quotes, switch/case) fails. This is a narrower acceptance boundary of an existing gate, not a separate obligation; recorded as a facet.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

distinguishing_scenario: Register dependency-guard for PreToolUse once with matcher Bash and once with matcher PowerShell: both tools covered, checker fails; a single Bash|PowerShell group passes.
facet_text: Each required event/script must be registered in a single group whose matcher (split on '|') contains every required tool, or whose matcher is empty/'*'/absent; coverage spread across several groups fails the check.
rationale: check-instructions.mjs:318-327 verified: groups.some(group => tools.every(...) && group runs script). FG-M-54d1e6e5e9 lists the required registrations ('on Bash|PowerShell') but not that coverage must sit in one group. Split registrations that cover every tool fail; recorded as an acceptance-boundary facet of the existing required-registration group.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

distinguishing_scenario: paths: ["backend/**/*.cs"] instead of a dash list: an intended non-empty list, but the checker reports 'frontmatter must declare a non-empty paths list'.
facet_text: The checker accepts a rule's paths only as a block sequence (paths: with an empty value followed by indented '- ' items); a flow sequence such as paths: ["x"] is parsed as a scalar and fails the non-empty paths-list check.
rationale: check-instructions.mjs:395-405 (parseYamlSubset: a non-empty scalar value becomes a string; only an empty value followed by '- ' lines yields an array) and 149-152 (Array.isArray check) verified. FG-M-948f3cb013 requires 'a non-empty paths list' without the representation boundary; a YAML flow sequence is a list in YAML but fails here. Facet, not a new rule; no claim about how Claude Code itself parses paths.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

target_group_original.neutral_claim_text: .claude/rules/ must be flat, contain only Markdown, and each rule must declare a non-empty paths list.

distinguishing_scenario: Headless run whose 'Proceeding with' is 'nothing' pauses for an approval that cannot arrive instead of finishing with the unresolved-request report: forbidden by the source; only implied by the group.

evidence.exact_excerpt:
In an autonomous or headless run, do not wait and do not decide: continue only
with the "Proceeding with" work and list every unresolved Decision Request in
the final report.
evidence.quote:
In an autonomous or headless run, do not wait and do not decide: continue only
with the "Proceeding with" work and list every unresolved Decision Request in
the final report.

facet_text: In an autonomous or headless run the agent does not wait for a decision response, also when no compliant work remains; it continues only with the 'Proceeding with' work and reports.
rationale: architecture-decision/SKILL.md:37-39 verified: 'do not wait and do not decide'. FG-M-2b1be76983 cites exactly these lines and states 'never make a Reserved decision; proceed only on a compliant non-Reserved path and report', so 'do not decide' is explicit while 'do not wait' is only implied. Making the timing part explicit is newly recorded granularity of the same obligation (protocol F6: text cited by both members, not contradicted), not new behaviour.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

target_group_original.neutral_claim_text: In an autonomous/headless run never make a Reserved decision; proceed only on a compliant non-Reserved path and report every unresolved Decision Request.

distinguishing_scenario: Known-key selection exists but a two-branch explicit factory is clearer: FG-M-01a562919a and FG-M-82d9796c78 allow keyed services; the source excludes them.

evidence.exact_excerpt:
Use keyed services when multiple implementations of the same abstraction are
selected by a known key, not when a normal single registration or a simple
explicit factory is clearer.
evidence.quote:
Use keyed services when multiple implementations of the same abstraction are
selected by a known key, not when a normal single registration or a simple
explicit factory is clearer.

facet_text: Even when implementations are selected by a known key, keyed services are not used when a normal single registration or a simple explicit factory is clearer.
rationale: dependency-injection/SKILL.md:76-78 verified. FG-M-01a562919a cites lines 76-78 but keeps only 'only when implementations are selected by a known key' and drops 'not when a normal single registration or a simple explicit factory is clearer'. FG-M-82d9796c78 ('only when they solve an actual composition problem') does not express the clarity exclusion. The omitted half adds a genuine exclusion to an existing group, so it is a facet rather than a new clause; Codex's NOVEL label is not confirmed.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

target_group_original.neutral_claim_text: Use keyed services only when implementations are selected by a known key; decorators when the same cross-cutting behaviour wraps an abstraction; assembly scanning only for genuinely repetitive registration and over the assembly that owns the services.
